idiom_name: composable query structure (predicate tree) + dialect interpreter + mapping metadata
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: model the query as a tree of nodes (source, join, predicate with and/or/not, projection, ordering, limit) and build it through factory methods that return new nodes instead of mutating one; keep SQL strings and values out of the tree, carrying values as named bind parameters beside it. A renderer walks the tree against a target dialect to produce a parameterised statement, and the mapper resolves class and field names through mapping metadata. What replaces the classic Query class in most stacks is a framework that already ships this surface (expression trees, criteria APIs, relation objects); build the structure by hand only when the stack has none.
code_sketch:
q = query(source=Customer)
   .where(eq(field('status'), param('status')))
   .where(ge(field('age'), param('min_age')) if min_age else no_op())
   .order(field('name'))
   .limit(50)
sql, params = render(q, dialect=postgres)
objects = mapper.map(session.execute(sql, params), Customer)
pitfalls: Letting the query object store values instead of parameters, so rendering interpolates them.
Sharing one mutable builder instance across requests, so clauses leak between queries.
Caching rendered SQL (or a session-bound query) under a table name instead of the query's identity.
Wrong move: concatenate request values into a query string -> attacker-controlled input changes SQL semantics -> instead bind values through parameter expressions and the execution API.

Wrong move: treat a QuerySet, Select or CriteriaQuery as durable detached data -> session or framework-version state becomes invalid or changes unexpectedly -> instead serialize a stable filter specification and rebuild the query in the target context.
Wrong move: assert only the in-memory predicate tree -> renderer or dialect mapping can emit wrong SQL -> instead inspect generated SQL and parameters and run a representative integration check.
